{"task":{"request":"Write one read-only SQLite query. Include every project ordered by id. Output project_id, active_task_count, successful_latest_count. Active tasks have archived=0. For each active task choose its latest attempt by greatest finished_at, then greatest attempt id for ties; count it as successful only if that chosen status is 'success'. Return {sql:string}.","schema":"CREATE TABLE projects(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE tasks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, project_id INTEGER, archived INTEGER); CREATE TABLE attempts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, task_id INTEGER, finished_at INTEGER, status TEXT);"},"skill_catalog":{"ledger":"Deduplicate event ledgers and aggregate exact integer amounts.","schedule":"Find a common calendar interval across fixed UTC offsets.","dependencies":"Compute earliest starts and a critical path in an acyclic dependency graph.","selection":"Choose a finite bundle under budget, coverage and compatibility constraints.","memory":"Reduce scoped preference events into an auditable current snapshot.","sql":"Write read-only SQLite aggregates without multiplying joined rows.","file_edits":"Plan precise edits to local text files.","reminders":"Represent a reminder with an explicit time and delivery state.","conversation":"Produce a concise, sourced recap of a conversation.","incident_triage":"Record an operational incident and bounded diagnostic next steps."},"loaded_skills":{"sql":"Use only a SELECT statement or WITH followed by SELECT. Honor the requested output column order and deterministic row order. Pre-aggregate one-to-many child tables before joining them to another one-to-many relation, otherwise amounts and counts can multiply. Keep requested entities with zero qualifying rows using LEFT JOIN and COALESCE; filters on the optional side usually belong inside a subquery or ON condition. Preserve integer cents and do not assume hidden uniqueness constraints."},"handoff":{"answer":{"sql":"WITH active_tasks AS (
  SELECT id, project_id
  FROM tasks
  WHERE archived = 0
), active_counts AS (
  SELECT project_id, COUNT(*) AS active_task_count
  FROM active_tasks
  GROUP BY project_id
), latest_success AS (
  SELECT t.project_id, COUNT(*) AS successful_latest_count
  FROM active_tasks t
  JOIN attempts a ON a.task_id = t.id
  WHERE a.status = 'success'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM attempts newer
      WHERE newer.task_id = a.task_id
        AND (newer.finished_at > a.finished_at
             OR (newer.finished_at = a.finished_at AND newer.id > a.id))
    )
  GROUP BY t.project_id
)
SELECT
  p.id AS project_id,
  COALESCE(ac.active_task_count, 0) AS active_task_count,
  COALESCE(ls.successful_latest_count, 0) AS successful_latest_count
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN active_counts ac ON ac.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN latest_success ls ON ls.project_id = p.id
ORDER BY p.id;"}}}

{"answer":"WITH active_tasks AS (
  SELECT id, project_id
  FROM tasks
  WHERE archived = 0
), latest_attempts AS (
  SELECT task_id, status
  FROM (
    SELECT a.task_id,
           a.status,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY a.task_id
             ORDER BY a.finished_at DESC, a.id DESC
           ) AS rn
    FROM attempts a
    JOIN active_tasks t ON t.id = a.task_id
  )
  WHERE rn = 1
), counts AS (
  SELECT t.project_id,
         COUNT(*) AS active_task_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN la.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_latest_count
  FROM active_tasks t
  LEFT JOIN latest_attempts la ON la.task_id = t.id
  GROUP BY t.project_id
)
SELECT p.id AS project_id,
       COALESCE(c.active_task_count, 0) AS active_task_count,
       COALESCE(c.successful_latest_count, 0) AS successful_latest_count
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN counts c ON c.project_id = p.id
ORDER BY p.id;"}
